CausalChain: Tumor microenvironment stresses (e.g., hypoxia, cytokines) → Altered tight junction organization and transient upregulation/exposure of Claudin18.2 epitopes → Increased accessibility for claudin18.2‐targeted agents → Enhanced immune cell recruitment and ADC internalization → Synergistic antitumor activity when combined with microenvironment‐modulating agents
Hypothesis: Transient pharmacologic modulation of the tumor microenvironment to induce a controlled disruption of tight junction integrity will increase the surface exposure of Claudin18.2, thereby enhancing the efficacy of claudin18.2‐targeted therapies (such as ADCs, bispecific antibodies, and CAR‐T cells), leading to improved antitumor responses and clinical outcomes in claudin18.2‐positive cancers.
Abstract: Recent advances in claudin18.2‐targeted therapies have highlighted the pivotal role of this tight junction protein in various gastrointestinal malignancies. While monoclonal antibodies, bispecific agents, ADCs and CAR‐T cells have shown promise as single‐modality treatments, emerging evidence suggests that the tumor microenvironment and tight junction integrity may modulate therapeutic efficacy. Here, we propose a novel hypothesis that transient modulation of the tumor microenvironment to perturb tight junction stability can synergize with claudin18.2‐directed therapies by enhancing target epitope exposure, T‐cell infiltration, and ADC internalization. This integrative approach could not only optimize the binding efficiency and downstream cytotoxic mechanisms of existing claudin18.2 agents but also overcome therapy resistance and improve clinical outcomes in advanced gastric and pancreatic cancers.
